what: has_unpack_to_dest_fp32<input_dfb,pack_default>() was defined TWICE (byte-identical duplicate blocks). Any kernel including tilize_helpers.hpp failed to compile with "redefinition of template ..." on all three TRISCs, so compute_kernel_lib::tilize was unusable out of the box. Cost a full compile-fail debug cycle before the first kernel could run at all, and blocks every future op that uses the tilize helper (toy_tilize_untilize is equally broken).
suggest: Delete the duplicate definition upstream (fixed in this run) and add a compile smoke test that includes each kernel_lib header from a trivial kernel, so a duplicated/broken header is caught by CI rather than by the first op to use it.

what: --profile is documented (agent prompt + /perf-measure) as the way to get device kernel ns, but in this checkout run_safe_pytest.sh only sets PROFILE_MODE and preflights the tracy import — it never wraps PYTEST_CMD with python -m tracy. Result: tests run, exit PASS, and the script prints "WARNING: --profile set but this run produced no ops_perf_results CSV"; generated/profiler/ is never created. Burned ~4 device runs before I found the working recipe (in-process profiler: TT_METAL_DEVICE_PROFILER/MID_RUN_DUMP/CPP_POST_PROCESS env at module import + ttnn.ReadDeviceProfiler + ttnn.get_latest_programs_perf_data), which is only discoverable by reading tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/examples/test_double_buffer.py.
suggest: Either fix run_safe_pytest.sh to actually exec under tracy, or document the in-process profiler recipe inline in /perf-measure Layer A1 as the primary path (it needs no wrapper, works for underscore-prefixed benches, and gives per-variant ns directly).

what: The template shows only allocate_tensor_on_device(shape, dtype, layout, device, mem_config), which derives the padded shape from the logical one. Any op whose OUTPUT padded shape differs from tile-round(logical) — i.e. every padding op, which the tilize contract requires — cannot be expressed: TensorSpec/ttnn.Shape have no python binding for an explicit padded shape (TensorLayout::fromPaddedShape is C++-only). The working mechanism is ttnn.reshape(t, logical_shape, padded_shape), which is a zero-cost view (same buffer address, verified by probe) but is documented nowhere in the references and reads like a data-movement op.
suggest: Add a short section to generic_op_template (or memory-layouts) on producing an output whose logical shape != padded shape: allocate at the padded target, then ttnn.reshape(out, logical, padded) as a view — with the note that it is zero-copy when the padded shape is unchanged.

what: Two authorities disagree on Phase 0 scope. eval/prompts/tilize.txt pins Phase 0 SUPPORTED to use_multicore=False, pad_mode=none, dtype=bfloat16, rank=4; the acceptance test the task prompt calls THE SPEC (and requires to pass) exercises multicore, both CB depths, fp32/bf8b casts, ranks 2/3/5, and all three pad modes. Gating to the narrow rectangle would have failed the acceptance test outright. I resolved it by treating the acceptance test as binding and widening SUPPORTED to what I actually built, but a future agent can just as reasonably read it the other way and ship a Phase 0 that fails its own gate.
suggest: State the precedence explicitly in the implementer task prompt (e.g. "the acceptance test defines this phase’s SUPPORTED rectangle; the refinement queue’s Phase-0 list is advisory when the two differ"), or generate the acceptance test from the same Phase-0 SUPPORTED list the queue declares.
